\caption{Superseded in part by Table~\STabNineBounds{}: rows that use the withdrawn reassignments as reference are kept for the record. Odds ratios of flooding from effects injected into the observed labels, read with different no-effect references (exploratory, amendment 8). A: all ground nearest a water-related name; B: the part within 500\,m of the settlement; CA, CB: the same for a latent indicator of truly water-related names, drawn with the measured misreading rates. Base models fixed; replicates: A 50, B 50, CA 50, CB 50. Upper bound: the odds ratio at which the reference plus the mean injected gain reaches the upper 90\,\% limit of the observed increment; in parentheses, the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles over 2,000 resamples of the replicates (Monte Carlo interval); values above the simulated range (odds ratio 20) are marked $>$. The detectable odds ratio is the smallest $e^{\delta}$ at which $\Phi\{(\Delta\mathrm{BS}_{\mathrm{null}}+g(\delta))/\mathrm{SE}-1.96\}$ reaches 0.8, where $g(\delta)$ is the mean gain from the injected effect and SE the bootstrap standard error of the observed increment; it ignores the variance that refitting adds. Bounds with every model refitted are not given: that simulation (amendment 7) has no effect below an odds ratio of 1.65, and reading it on a straight line from zero across the convex gain curve would understate them; its gains were 0.91--0.95 of those with the base models fixed, so refitted bounds would be slightly larger (amendment 8, addendum 9).}\label{tab:eight-bounds}
